item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
My SCP is a rabbit that occasionally creates small balls of fur that are hostile towards humans or other animals when they feel threatened
They attack through means of forcing people to cuddle with them followed by hypnotizing them, causing them to seize all other activities.

Central Narrative:
The SCP is a white rabbit that was discovered in a park surrounded by a bunch of its created fur balls instances that were causing people to fall into hypnosis.
The foundation got notified about the event and came in to capture the SCP and terminate it furball instances. It is later revealed during research that the SCP has multiple anomalous effects and how to counter them.

This idea is something I haven’t read before on the wiki, and I think the idea tells a very interesting concept, seeing as its story fits with foundation lore.

item.title: Re: @fterlife.net (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Sorry writer, but you need a specific layout for the Ideas Critique Forum in order for it to be accepted.

Seeking Greenlights: Put yes or no.

Page Type: SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify)

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify)

Page Layout (Optional): How will you structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.

Elevator Pitch: What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.

Central Narrative: Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none". (Note that it is extremely rare for articles without narrative context or worldbuilding content to receive greenlights.)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?

Additional Notes: Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.

item.title: Re: any suggestions for my SCP?
item.content:encoded:
I'm not really a fan of the central narrative section; it feels…too expected and too focussed on the backstory of this. My general advice when writing a SCP is to forget about why it exists (and how the Foundation found it, a little). In general, backstory is not the most interesting angle because it happens a) before the foundation get involved (and so, before any of the PoV characters can be there) and b) it's just, not very interesting; and this suffers from this a lot since there's not really any way for the Foundation to know about the mans' gradual discovery of his powers, not a lot happens while he discovers them, and it's very temporally removed from the here and now and the people involved in the story.

item.title: SCP "Darkhouse" - [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Terminal / SCP Historical

Page Layout (Optional): Discovery (audio recordings; scanned original documents; terminal)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Perhaps there was a reason why the O5-Council decided to bury this information…

Elevator Pitch:
+ Open
- Close

A Junior Researcher logs onto an older terminal and uncovers a forgotten SCP with deep roots in the SCP foundations history.


Central Narrative:
+ Open
- Close

The SCP foundation has a questionable history, but this Junior Researcher attempts to solidify one of the oldest SCPs discovered by the Foundation. Compiling information from older terminals and transcribing paper archives, the SCP “Darkhouse” is reclassified as one of the earliest discovered SCPs. The SCP was “lost” when the Foundation transferred their data from paper to computers.

Dating back to 1792, the original Cape Henry Lighthouse was the first federally funded public works project of the newly formed United States government. In 1881, a new lighthouse was constructed to replace the original. With rising threats from around the world, both human and anomalous, the United States government attempted to utilize unexplainable properties the original lighthouse possessed.

The SCP “Darkhouse” ‘s anomalous properties are charged by UVA (315-400 nm) and UVB (280-315 nm) Ultraviolet radiation. The radiation appears to activate the anomalous properties, causing the SCP “Darkhouse” to enter an “active” state. During this state, the SCP “Darkhouse” will project a photon-absorbing substance, blocking all light it encompasses. Effects of the substance on living organisms have been redacted due to its tendencies to dissolve and dissipate matter. Containment procedures have been automated and the SCP “Darkhouse” has not been attended to by Foundation personnel since its original containment.


Additional Notes: “It doesn’t shine, it shadows…”

item.title: Uncertain Unreality
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological… something

Page Layout (Optional): A normal SCP article, but it's split into two distinct sections

Elevator Pitch: The SCP itself is more or less the designation for two separate scenarios. In scenario A, the SCP is a Euclid SCP, who's a young human girl, a bit distorted from reality, and makes half of the people who know of her think she doesn't actually exist.
In scenario B, the SCP is an infohazardous memetic effect, which makes half of the people who know of it think that there's a person there, who really isn't.
The memetic effect of either scenario is so powerful, and so overwhelming, that despite their best efforts, the foundation can't tell which one is true, so they've documented it as if it's neither and both at the same time.
After all, it's impossible to prove either way

Central Narrative: The main narrative is gonna come from how the scenario A SCP is mentally affected by her affliction, and how she may have gotten like this based on interviews with her and the like
Also, it's going to focus on how this uncertainty is affecting the foundation personnel who know of the SCP, including conflicts starting due to people in scenario A starting fights with people in scenario B
People are getting angry about a whole humanoid containment chamber which is going completely unused

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the main hook is obviously the esoterics of something that can't be proven to exist or not exist, and possibly how the foundation reacts to encountering something that they can't truly understand despite their best efforts. I'd imagine people would already be interested as soon as they see "Object Class: Euclid / Keter (?)"

Additional Notes: I guess above all else I want to know if this concept has been done before and if so I would like to know how to make it more unique.
Also, I just wanna know if it's good or not alltogether

item.title: Skeleton's Daycare
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: I don't really know, maybe a bit emotional in some parts?

  • Elevator Pitch
  • Central Narrative
  • Hook/Attention Grabber
  • Additional Notes

It's a daycare owned by a living skeleton. The skeleton itself isn't anomalous (though it can talk, which skeletons aren't able to do, but that's about it), it's just a normal human who decomposed into a skeleton but is still alive due to some crystals on the walls.

There's no other staff in the daycare, but what they do have are alien children to take care of. For the most part, they're fairly normal. They have a bit of a temper, but that's just kids being kids. They are capable of causing minor earthquakes though, so you might not wanna anger them too badly.

This daycare used to be pretty normal. Then these alien parents came in and had to drop their kids off because "they had to do something (translation: they were being abandoned)." When they left the kids at the daycare, they left them with some crystals that would make them immortal.

Two people used to run the daycare, but the original owner left to go find the parents because they've been gone for way too long and they can't close without all the kids leaving. This left the other guy to run it all by himself, but the owner was out for so long that the other guy's body died and became a skeleton.

After some time, one of the alien parents came back and took their kid, along with one of the crystals. This caused the skeleton's life to become much harder. This, along with the stress of taking care of aliens, was adding up.

At some point, the skeleton couldn't take it anymore and just left the building, causing him to die from getting out of range from the crystals. The children were attached to him after living there for a long time, so they tried to bring him inside and get him to live again, but it didn't work. Remember in the Elevator Pitch how the kids could cause minor earthquakes? They're really upset now, and they're causing serious damage to the rest of the world. They tried calming them down, but nothing would work. Because of the danger and the fact that the parents weren't coming back, they had to neutralize them.

A daycare slowly going into ruins.

[Note from the owner: Kill me.]

item.title: Please don't stare
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, History.

Page Layout (Optional): Probably a good chunk of the article will be filled with dialogues.

Elevator Pitch: a humanoid SCP cursed with a deadly beauty: anyone that makes eye contact cannot feel happiness after that, slowly losing the will to live. The physical aspect of the SCP is different for each person.

Central Narrative: This being would be discovered when the suicide rate of a small town began to show astronomic growth. When brought to the foundation site, a scientist would open the eyes and bring a curse to 5 foundation personnel. The SCP would cooperate with the foundation to try and find a solution, but no amnestics would work and the five would eventually die of starvation or commit suicide, leaving the SCP crying on the corner of it’s cell. Following this tragic event, a series of cold-hearted tests would be performed, including sending many D-class personnel to stare at it’s eyes. The O-5 council decided to shut down the tests for being “too cruel” and the tests would now only be performed in case of someone accidentally staring the creature.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Testing on the SCP would show superhuman strength and resistance, as well as high knowledge in diverse areas and an extensive vocabulary, including many different languages. The SCP would have its own personality, portrayed by the “logs” of his conversation between the scientists, and it loves someone to read a book to it. This SCP is a pacifist, knocking out the opponents instead of killing them (this would be proven in the few containment breaches of his).

Additional Notes: I hadn’t come with a cool name yet. Also, if anyone finds an existing SCP with a similar concept, please notify.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight for first SCP: True NPC
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): (meta) Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Two variants of the article, one describing the SCP upon discovery and initial tests, the other after learning about it's true scope

Elevator Pitch: Self aware NPC attempts to break out to the real world, after Foundation tries to contain it, and learns about multi-layered nature of the Foundation reality, created specifically to stop pataphysical threats

Central Narrative: Foundation learns about the existence of a self aware character from roleplaying games, whose name is a cognitohazard, that forces people perceiving it to include this character in their roleplaying activities. They try to contain it, like any other memetically spreading SCP, but it did not want to have its freedom restricted, so it decided to break out to the real world. Foundation, prepared for this kind of pataphysical dangers, created beforehand many layers of fictional realities, each identical to the top one, with Earth, Foundation and all the jazz, to contain entities traveling upwards through layers of fictional realities.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Afaik there are no skips going "upwards'' through the reality layers, besides SCP-3812, who accidently went from our reality one level higher, but we don't have any coming from "below" and on purpose. Similarly, there is a multitude of fictional (from the in-universe point of view) SCPs but not much connected to the roleplaying (books and computer games get the majority of attention in this area afaik). I'm also planning on exploring limits of the mentioned cognitohazard, and the entity itself through test logs (something I see rather rarely, but find personally fascinating).

Additional Notes: English is not my first language (as you can probably tell) and I'll be thankful for pointing any misspellings or grammar mistakes. Also I never before used any »real« internet forum more complicated than facebook or reddit, so I'm sorry in advance for my mistakes while trying to make sense of it (I hope that I created this post in the right way). Thanks for reading, I hope you will like my idea, and maybe I'll manage to get the greenlight for my first SCP ^^

item.title: Re: The Grave Of A Chief
item.content:encoded:
Hi, yes Id be happy to elaborate! 400 words is a little restrictive.

The mountains were actually giants yes, the entire mountain range is the bodies of these giants who were slain in the war. And the tribes were reality benders yes but comparativley weak at it compared to other reality benders since its an aquired power and not something they have inherently like a "true" reality bender (if there even is a criteria.)

+ Show
- Close

I was unable to include it in the main post but the war was initiated by the common "betrayal of god" story of many indigenous tribes which is similar somewhat to the tower of babylon in that all animals and humans and gods used to speak a common language until humanity betrays their god(s). They often (though not in all tribes) fight a war between the animals and humans in which they always lose and are forced to migrate to what ever their home is when they tell the story.

though god in the sense its understood in indigenous stories is that they are limitless in knowledge and in creation but they are unable to control anything they create outside of outsmarting them, since self determinism itself is something thats impossible to override, even for gods. Which is why they are forced to talk to humans occassionally.

As for how the giant mythos, the betrayal of god and war tie to the tribe being able to bend reality and sacrificing it,
the tribe sacrificed their reality bending powers to keep the mountain they now call chief mountain from dying in the war that resulted from their betrayal of god. This tribe, who saved the chief mountain, are one of the few tribes who werent forced to migrate as the mountain sacrificed itself to kill the rest of the giants which is why the tribe sacrificed their reality bending to keep it alive, since they couldnt save it completely you can think of it as them keeping the mountain on life support through both the sacrifice of intial reality bending powers and continued rituals.

the mountain isnt contained by this initial sacrifice, i guess neutralized would maybe fit better but i was unsure if that would still apply if the anomoly wasnt fully neutralized and still posed a threat eventually. All the sacrifice did was keep the mountain from dying of its own sacrifice for the tribe, which was to protect them from the other giants and animals from the war.

The political gains part is that the mountain is still a strong ally of the small tribe and if you were a small group who lost a war to an empire and were gifted essentially a weapon of mass destruction, the literal power of a mountain to weild at your will. would you not become mad with power? would you not attempt to assert your power and claim your own piece of the pie? I thought it only seemed natural as every tribe in real life sees themselves as nations in conflict with whatever country they live in (US, Canada, mexico, etc) so if you have the nation vs nation mindset and got incredible power, asserting that power politically would naturally follow.

so the foundation needs to contain the mountain in one of a few ways, containing it in conjunction to the tribe, contain it without the tribes involvment at all or if nothing else killing it. This is where the political aspect comes into play again, the foundation needs to make sure the entity is contained to its area. Though they eventually realize that even if the tribe were appeased, and in the best case scenario, they werent greedy and only took a small area for their nation. The mountain itself is still autonomous so the foundation is unsure if the mountain could be kept perpetually contained by the tribes persuasion to it, as in the past humanity, and the tribes in particular, have their history of betraying their god. So they could potentially betray the mountain and cause the foundation to lose their , potentially only means of containing it
so the foundation is torn between just circumventing the tribe all together and risking expending massive resources to potentially contain something but with the benefit thay if they do, itll be perpetually. as opposed to appeassing the tribe which is a known way to contain the entity, low on resources and could buy some time, but also isnt garunteed to last forever, essentially its a bandaid solution.

Sorry if thats alot to read, i hope you better understand how everything ties together. If you still dont understand ill try to work the story into a less complex and more focused story but i wanted to be able to explain alot of the seemingly unconnected ideas that a come to form the larger arc and not just the specific story in this specific time period, i wanted to include past and future events in some capacity.

Please collapse long posts - Staff

item.title: A Simple Bar
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Interview logs and also a log about when the bar manifested and when the Foundation sent an MTF in to determine if the place is a threat

Elevator Pitch: A "simple" bar and owner of said bar, that has the ability to hop across dimensions in order to serve as many customers as possible. Said bar
sets up shop just outside a Foundation site in the middle of nowhere in the hopes of making more money.

Central Narrative:
+Block
-Block

The bartender and owner is relatively open and talkative about the people he's met and places he's been, but when the foundation start trying to find out
some of the more personal questions about his and the bars history he starts getting more dismissive and less talkative. My idea is that the Owner used to run the place with his brother until they traveled to a dimension they weren't welcome in, with the consequence being that the brother is kept half dead, bloody, and basically soulless chained up in the back room of the bar. The owner is unable to let his brother die and let himself move on, so he pays the strange man who lives in the dimension a fee every month for him to help keep his brother alive. In an attempt to make as much money as he can to pay the strangers increasing demands he puts his bar down next to a very busy Foundation site. The interviews with foundation staff start fine with the owner happily telling stories and chatting, but each interview he gets more and more reserved and disturbed with hints and clues as to his brothers fate, until just before an interview the owner comes out from the backroom with blood on his hands with tears in his eyes.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What I'm trying to go for is it starting all happy with stories and fun banter and slowly see it turn into horror.

Additional Notes: I plan on leaving most of the history of the place only hinted at so the reader could speculate and come to their own conclusions.

item.title: Re: What makes the Foundation the Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
So what makes the foundation once you strip away the O5 council and the researchers?

In addition to the Council and Research/Development, the Foundation also has a lot of administrative and military infrastructure. The Council is generally understand as kinds of "eyes in the sky", but in their absence each site would exercise regional oversight and probably have the manpower to maintain the status quo. Big picture stuff, like making some world-saving weapon or another, requires some level of comprehensive knowledge of the anomalous and research/development.

If you were to ask me "What is the Foundation's essense?" I'd probably respond that it's their particular dogma. Research and containment, essentially. The Council, researchers, and nearly everything else is built on maintaining a status quo.

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Mirror Cyborgs
item.content:encoded:
Good notes, I'll go back to what worked and come up with alternatives for what did not work.

But about Anderson, yes it's been stated how he uses magic, but where did that magic come from? If Methane is the god of machines, I mean not just a giant robot that claims to be a god but actually a divine entity that can actually be defined as a god, then wouldn't it be possible that Anderson's technology could fall under his domain? I was actually coming at this from a "God works in mysterious ways" approach, maybe Anderson didn't realize he was taking the power of a god when he first found his magic, but what he did still got the God's attention.

As for the plot holes around 3560, I thought about that. I believe it hasn't actually been found yet so it's claims would refer to a place that the Foundation isn't aware of yet, so it would refer to it's world in a more oblique way that makes sense to the reader but not to the in universe characters, at least not yet. Also, yes the inhabitants turn intangible when removed, but there is evidence that there are exceptions when they go hunting individuals for a reason. 2806 isn't made with the awareness that they are pulling from that dimension(Vincent and Phone as were working off studying magic without realizing the methods would summon spirits from another dimension to animate their creations or that the other dimension would come back for them), although Vincent himself suggests that tracking similar energy would help the Foundation track the instances still unaccounted for which means he may at least suspect a connection even if he's not aware. So the idea was that 2806 is animated by 3560, which is why they appear in disrepair, the parts of their souls are being borrowed to animate partial robotics. Imagine that saying "Integrate" to activate the Gyrfalcon actually summons a robot spirit to inhabit the physical construct. It would be like Taily-po, and the rest of the robot spirit is trying to get his Taily-po and is able to come get him the same way the other spirits would later come to take the Anderson traitors and thus be an exception that remains tangible because it has a specific tie to something in this world.

I thought I had this thought out, I've been researching this for two months and I thought I had this worked out. If I missed something important please provide a link. If I can't work around this, I will remove Anderson altogether and start this over as completely original, but I wanted to tie together existing lore. Every time I read a cyborg article with unclear origins I wonder who made this thing because it had to be made by someone and then Anderson and CotBG seem to cover it well and any SCP that strays makes me wonder what poor soul is making these machines and will they ever find their home in the universe with the other anomalous machines?

Central Narrative: I haven't really thought of this, and to be honest I don't think I really need one.

You do need one yeah; you're trying to write a short story about a weird thing, not an encylcopedia entry on it; and so what you do with the anomaly is more important than what the anomaly does.

I want to include a long list of experimentations referencing other space-related SCPs, and possibly hint at some side effects / alternate anomalous properties this object might have along the way.

So like, what are the side effects? What are the alternate anomalous properties? What other space-related SCPs? What's tying your experiments together so it feels like a cohesive whole and not just a random series of experiments?

My central concern is that as far as anomalous stuff goes, this almost feels more like an anomalous item: it has a very simple thing what it does and there's not a lot of like, things you can do to explore it. The hinting towards experiment logs could be enough to fix this but honestly I don't really have enough of a feel for what you're doing with them or how you're wanting them to be funny to tell if it'd work.

item.title: Re: Myantharun's Mandala-Manifested Meadow of Majestic, Melancholic Madness
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

The discovery section doesn't actually mention the SCP at all. Like, there's not even anything which like is referenced as a mandala or anything so it just kinda feels weird?

This means the addendum in the first iteration doesn't flow right because we haven't seen a SCP-XXXX mandala yet so there's not a clear thing that the dream team can like…do to go to SCP-XXXX-1?

The second iteration feels really unsatisfying as a whole: it feels like it doesn't quite build off the first one in a way that grants closure so much as is just kinda…confusing? Like, idk, I guess my question is why a SCP file for this anomaly exists but Dream Team aren't made aware of what Ara Orun are up to; or well, really, why the conflict between the two continues like why don't they just talk to each other? It's not like one of these files is more classified than the other, at least according to the ACS.

I like the first iteration generally; it feels lacking as a whole but it has some really nice 'descent into dreamland' vibes and I enjoy it; but iteration 2 doesn't really build off it so much as feel like it's the narrative equivalent of hitting a brick wall while you're going at 90 on the highway?

This said: it also feels a lot like this is a kinda generic dream entity and I'm not sure if that's just because I don't really get what's happening here on a metaphorical level?

Coherence

Mostly fine; it feels like it's all kinda centred around a single thing and escalation situation and stuff; a few things I've mentioned above are a little iffy from this perspective too but they're relatively easily to fix.

Consistency

Not quite sure what you mean by this; but the internal logic of the piece feels like it's being kept consistent and the rules aren't suddenly changing or anything.

Dialogue

It's fine? There's not really any lines that stand out as being hugely memorable or anything; but there's equally no lines which feel hugely clunky or anything.

The characters could perhaps do with more of a personality: they're like, obviously different because of what they can do but they aren't all that different in terms of how they talk or what they're like as people.

Clinical tone

Yeah basically fine. See the LBL for some minor things.

Pacing & Plot & Second list page

See earlier comments.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

SCP-XXXX and its related anomalies are undetectable by most individuals without sufficient anti-memetics training, therefore standard visual containment is not required.

'related anomalies' feels vague here in an unsatisfying way: do you mean -1 and -2? do you mean a whole bunch of other antimemetic SCPs?

Also, I'm not necessarily sure that the lack of visual containment does necessarily follow here? Like I'm sure it does when a reader sees the actual properties and stuff; but in this isolated bit, it stands out as weird because like…we can still be affected by stuff we can't detect (e.g., if you drain all the air out a room, we might not be able to see that but we can certainly be affected by it).

This particularly feels janky when the next sentence implies it can be seen sometimes! So why don't they lock it up just in case?

In rare circumstances, such as under the influence of psychedelics, visibility of SCP-XXXX is possible.

"In rare circumstances,…, SCP-XXXX can be visually detected.' would probably flow better: 'visibility' feels like a gradient rather than a binary, and possible feels iffy when talking gradients.

are to be amnesticized and monitored for any significant and abrupt changes

'significant or abrupt' might be better here but but *shrugs*

as well as for signs of psychosis

SCP-XXXX Is an anomalous mandala

rogue capital

a graphic and often symbolic pattern usually in the form of a circle divided into four separate sections or bearing a multiple projection of an image.

'bearing a multiple projection of an image' is janky but I'm not exactly sure how best to fix it

I would also generally lean towards capitalising the first word of a footnote.

that has been observed appearing in multiple population centers.

I feel like this is a touch vague about what it actually is? Like is it just…an image that appears a lot in posters? Is it a weird 2d image entity that moves around?

Every instance of SCP-XXXX is identical in pattern, coloration and size.

this feels a little unsatisfying because it's never actually like, described in any way: like I get putting an image of it in the file is probably a bad idea but like…there's not even a vague description of what it includes.

SCP-XXXX-2 is an entity of varying form that is located in SCP-XXXX-1. Its form is that a young humanoid woman with wings on its back that resemble those of a blue butterfly. (Blue Morpho)

Does it have varying form or is it's form that of a young woman with wings on its back that resemble those of a blue butterfly?

IMO: you can cut humanoid here; if you say 'young woman', people will assume 'human' or at least 'human adjacent'.

I'd also have the 'blue morpho' before the full stop; or potentially as the main text with a footnote explaining it's a butterfly

MTF Omicron Rho ("The Dream Team") discovered SCP-XXXX-2 in their deployment into SCP-XXXX-1. See addenda.

I'd probably cut this since the conflation between this and the discovery right after feels…confusing? Like in the sense that this introduces a second discovery event right before you introduce the first.

When the congregation underwent substantial changes in behavior while the parishioners were in prayer.

This is a sentence fragment that's missing what happened when said substantial changes occurred.

Another significant portion of the congregation attempted

I feel like specifying an approximate number instead of 'significant' would be more effective here.

to eat portions of the marble pews3 Traces of blood and fragments of broken teeth were discovered at the site of this incident.

this footnote is unnecessary and you're missing a period.

I also feel like the flow of information is weird: I think noting that it's hypothesised that people tried to eat the pews based of the blood/teeth fragments at the site would work better; or like, indicating that the eating caused there to be said traces left or something.

After this incident, the Foundation dispatched field agents to survey the surroundings

This phrasing kinda implies that the Foundation knew about the incident in some magical manner and immediately dispatched agents after it occurred; it feels like this needs an intermediate step like e.g. embedded agents in the police department diverting this to the foundation or something.

I'd also be tempted to put a number of agents in here; or refer to a single field agent say.

Their comms devices were discovered drenched in an unseen fluid that could only be detected by Foundation psychics.

This feels weird to me; like, the further in we get, the less saying they were discovered 'drenched' feels like it makes sense. Also 'unseen' is unnecessary if only psychics can detect it; it implies it could be e.g. felt whereas the later part indicates it can't even be felt.

Exploration Video Log Transcript

I'd probably trim the 'exploration team' and 'subject' fields and instead add a short summary of the purpose of this: like, why are Omicron Rho being sent in? Is their job 'to identify anomalies within SCP-XXXX-1' or 'to explore -1' or 'to recover someone from -1' or?

Dream Team moves toward locked wooden door.

IMO: not having a 'The' at the start here feels a little wonky.

House, Hero and Operator lean against the wall next to the door.

Listing the names like this implies there's more team members than just those three here

They slowly open the door and peer through the crack.

This was described as a 'locked wooden door' a second earlier; how are they opening it now?

The nun walks over to the door and opens it.

What door is this? The only one mentioned has already been opened?

Operator: <Operator takes several pictures of the fluid and saves them to her folder.>

FOOTAGE LOST

I'd probably centre this

<Operator slowly approaches a sedated young woman.

Missing the > at the end here

save for a Mandala symbol that appears tattooed onto its face

Is this a SCP-XXXX mandala or a different mandala?

//<Hero turns around, telekinetically lifts chunks of dirt and rocks out of the ground and throwing them into the distance.

Missing the closing > and //

This action, and the following stuff, feels…completely disconnected from what was happening just before it in a slightly unsatisfying way

Dream Team appears in what resembles medieval Europe

'appears somewhere that resembles' might parse better here

House: <Erects a brick wall from the ground, stopping a citizen who was mid-flight.>

IMO: cut the dialogue tag and just use the action but with 'House' at the start.

Then again, this just…feels odd for House to do?

Operator pulls House by the collar of his fatigues and pulls him backwards.

I'd change the first 'pulls' to 'grabs', or cut the 'and pulls him' and move 'backwards' to just after 'House'.

House's leg gets caught in the serpent's form,

How does it get caught? This feels weirdly passive

Operator: <Operator continues dragging House.>

Probably the last time I'll mention this but the dialogue tag can be cut here and anywhere you do this.

launching every citizen around him.

this feels like it's missing something like 'into the air' at the end; like, words indicating where the citizens go, y'know?

Hero frees himself from the large man's hold

this feels weirdly lacking in description of how it's done

standing underneath an instance of SCP-XXXX.

this is altogether far too far into this SCP for this to be the first explicitly mentioned instance of SCP-XXXX (there's been a few mandalas that could be the scp but nothing concrete)

<SCP-XXXX-2 steps back and stares at the stone circle.>//

missing opening //

FOOTAGE LOST

the last one in the document is missing the lines before/after it.

Iteration 1

Mobile Task Force Omega-0 ("Ará Orún") is to be deployed into SCP-XXXX-1 by using SCP-XXXX as entryways.

deployed into -1 to do what?

SCP-XXXX-3 is to be forcibly contained within SCP-XXXX-1 and redirected back into SCP-XXXX-2.

Something about the flow of this feels janky; but I think it's just that we haven't had the new -1 and -2 established so -2 being a thing that exists in -1 isn't like,,, something we're sure of yet?

All efforts are to be focused on a permanent solution to SCP-XXXX-2's rapidly deteroriating condition.

I feel like something more specific than 'rapidly deteriorating condition' would be good here: really show what's happening in an evocative way, y'know?

Its primary locations for spawning include but are not limited to

something about this feels iffy; maybe "It primarily appears in the following locations:" would be better?

  • Mass congregations.
  • Cults.

These feel…vague for locations?

SCP-XXXX is the pathway between SCP-XXXX-1 and reality.

My general feeling is that you have to say what -1 is before you can say this; perhaps saing e.g. "pathway between the collective unconsciousness (designated SCP-XXXX-1) and reality" would be best?

Addendum:

I would add line breaks between the paragraphs here just to space it out a little.

Hello hello SpookyBonez! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It seems that YouTube is quite the introduction power to this site; you'd be surprised how many people discover SCP through videos, and it's really awesome to see that we achieved such a wide audience. If you're going to push further in writing for the site, you'll want to click that little red collapsible at the bottom of this comment - there, you'll find a plethora of useful resources created for the purpose of guiding new members of the site towards guides and other resources which will definitely help you improve your writing and seek help on it.

Without further ado though, let's actually click it, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

We've got plenty upon plenty of different stories to go through, each weirder than the rest, which hopefully won't core you in a long time. It's also really awesome to see that you want to contribute on your own. You'll want to click that little red collapsible at the bottom of this comment - there, you'll find a plethora of useful resources created for the purpose of guiding new members of the site towards guides and other resources which will definitely help you improve your writing and seek help on it.

Without further ado though, let's actually click it, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Post-haste our illustrious Foundation secures the area and is now able to devote its energy to a favored past-time: testing logs. Including but not limited to logs from the personnel/civilians on the ground, and logs from the Foundation's bunker where testing can be conducted on D-Class in peace.

I guess my big concern is: what are these testing logs showing? It kinda feels like they might feel…pedestrian; but I think a few showcasing the various melodies it produces could be a fun little middle section.

We also have a neat little epilogue with the arrest of the two individuals responsible, and the return of the children to the foster care system.

Uhhh what children? Are they just a some children who are enamoured by the clock or?

become obsessive with the clock, and may begin to prioritize listening to the chime over basic bodily needs.

this feels to me like it's…perhaps a very dark turn for a supposedly light hearted scp to take

I don't necessarily hate the idea of this; and a lot of this feels like it comes close to working; but it feels like it's missing something to just really kick it over the line and I'm not quite sure what?

The test logs feeling awkwardly inserted between the discovery section and the epilogue might be the core issue; but it might be that there's not a huge feeling of purpose to this: it might just need some kinda hint as to why the two people responsible made this and what they were intending, y'know?
